stories.headline: OpenXR ratifies cross-platform spatial multitasking API
stories.subtitle: The Khronos Group published new OpenXR extensions bringing Apple-style spatial multitasking to Quest, Steam Frame, Android XR headsets, and XREAL glasses. Implementations roll out through 2026 — a quiet win for headset apps behaving more like real computers.

stories.headline: Virtuix now an official Meta reseller; Omni One Quest bundles ship
stories.subtitle: Virtuix sells its full-body Omni One treadmill with a Quest 3 ($599 extra) or Quest 3S ($349); the treadmill alone is $2,595. Orders are up roughly 3x since June, with 75+ Quest titles compatible — a talking point for VR-curious shoppers.

stories.headline: XREAL Aura priced at $1,279 — about $20 under Meta's VR Glasses
stories.subtitle: XREAL put a number on its long-teased Aura glasses this week: $1,279 base, roughly $20 less than Meta's $1,299.99 VR Glasses — both tested by The Verge and WIRED. The head-to-head for spring wearable VR is getting real, and customers comparing the two will cite this.

stories.headline: Valve software update boosts Steam Frame battery life up to 12%
stories.subtitle: Valve's update extends battery life up to 12% in standalone play and PC streaming, and improves streaming quality. Demand still outpaces supply — the order queue stretches into 2027, so set holiday expectations carefully if customers ask about the Frame.

stories.headline: Apple's next Vision Pro reportedly 'on life support', may never ship
stories.subtitle: Bloomberg's Mark Gurman reports Apple's next headset (codenamed N224) may never reach shelves, and its first smart glasses remain a 2027 play at the earliest. For customers weighing Apple vs Meta in VR, Meta's roadmap is currently the more certain one.
